design_summary.purpose: Synthesizable ASIC control-and-supervision IP for active aerodynamics. The block manages request launch, request/response validation, safety supervision, deterministic command synthesis, saturation, fallback selection, and telemetry around an external DoMINO service. It does not implement the physics or surrogate model itself and is intended to preserve deterministic safe behavior independent of external model availability.
design_summary.operating_model: The top-level qualifies control cycles using control_valid, vehicle_geometry_valid, and flow_conditions_valid, checks stream velocity against the configured operating envelope, and launches requests only when allowed. Outstanding transaction state is retained until a matching fresh response is accepted or a timeout/fault occurs. Accepted model outputs are converted by local hardware logic into a raw actuator command, then clamped to programmed limits and registered at the output. Safety supervision can force fallback command selection with priority over model-derived actuation, and telemetry records accepted, rejected, clamp, timeout, and fallback events.

module_architecture.name: active_aero_supervisor
module_architecture.role: Top-level control, validation, safety, request/response, telemetry, clamp, and fallback integration block for active aerodynamics.
responsibilities: Qualify outbound model requests using input-validity, envelope, and fallback-routing rules.
Generate and retain request ID, sequence, and timestamp for each outstanding transaction.
Accept only matching, fresh, well-formed responses.
Reject stale, malformed, mismatched, or timed-out responses without influencing actuator output.
Map accepted model outputs to a bounded actuator command word using local hardware logic.
Prioritize fallback command over model-derived command whenever fallback_active is asserted.
Expose safety status bits and sticky telemetry counters.
Guarantee registered actuator command output with no combinational path from response inputs to actuator outputs.
interface_notes: Receives the asynchronous model response transaction on model_response_valid and model_response_payload and exposes outbound request transaction data on model_request_valid and model_request_payload.
Outputs actuator_cmd_valid and actuator_cmd only from registered/supervised data, with fallback taking priority over model-derived command generation.
Accepts host configuration inputs for operating envelope refinement, freshness window, timeout policy, sticky clear, and fallback command selection.
ownership_notes: Top-level module name, ports, and file association are inherited from digital_spec_json without modification.
The top-level owns system-level arbitration between request management, response validation, command synthesis, clamp, safety, and telemetry.

module_architecture.name: request_manager
module_architecture.role: Request qualification, transaction ID/sequence generation, request payload formatting, and outstanding transaction tracking for the external DoMINO service.
responsibilities: Capture and increment request ID and sequence number only on qualified and granted launches.
Package geometry reference and stream velocity into the outbound request payload.
Assert request_valid_out only when a request is launched to the external service.
Hold outstanding request metadata until cleared by response acceptance or timeout.
Report envelope violations for safety supervision.
interface_notes: Consumes control_valid, vehicle_geometry_valid, flow_conditions_valid, stream_velocity_mps, geometry_ref, host_fallback_route_en, host_operating_en_min_mps, host_operating_en_max_mps, request_launch_grant, outstanding_clear, and request_valid_out as specified.
Produces request_id_out, request_seq_out, request_timestamp_out, request_payload_out, request_pending_out, and envelope_violation_out.
The request payload includes geometry reference and flow/velocity context in a deterministic encoded format.
ownership_notes: Owns request ID, sequence, timestamp, pending state, and request payload formatting for the transaction lifecycle.
No new request is issued while a prior request remains pending unless cleared or timed out.

module_architecture.name: response_validator
module_architecture.role: Asynchronous model response transaction validation and payload normalization block.
responsibilities: Check response request ID against the outstanding request ID.
Check response sequence against the outstanding sequence.
Check response age against the freshness window and timeout policy.
Parse drag_force, lift_force, surface_pressure, and flow_field metadata fields from the payload.
Assert explicit stale, invalid, and timeout indicators for supervisory consumption.
Provide normalized model-output words only on accepted responses.
interface_notes: Consumes model_response_valid, model_response_payload, outstanding_request_id, outstanding_request_seq, outstanding_timestamp, and freshness_window_cycles.

Produces response_accepted_out, response_stale_out, response_invalid_out, response_timeout_out, drag_force_out, lift_force_out, surface_pressure_out, flow_field_meta_out, and response_payload_valid_out.
A response is accepted only when request ID and sequence match and the response age is within the freshness window.
ownership_notes: Owns acceptance, stale, invalid, timeout, and parsed output qualification state for the external response channel.
Rejected responses do not update downstream command synthesis inputs.

module_architecture.name: command_synthesizer
module_architecture.role: Deterministic local hardware mapping from accepted model output words to a bounded actuator command word.
responsibilities: Generate a deterministic actuator command from accepted drag/lift/pressure/metadata inputs.
Select safe fallback command when fallback is active, with priority over model-derived commands.
Provide a raw command word for downstream clamping.
Indicate whether the current command source is fallback or model-derived.
interface_notes: Consumes response_payload_valid_in, drag_force_in, lift_force_in, surface_pressure_in, flow_field_meta_in, and fallback_active_in.
Produces command_raw_out, command_valid_out, command_source_fallback_out, and safe_fallback_command_in as specified.
Implements fixed local hardware logic, lookup tables, arithmetic, and scaling; it does not implement surrogate inference.
ownership_notes: Owns deterministic command synthesis behavior for the active-aerodynamics actuator domain.
Fallback command selection has priority over all model-derived outputs.

module_architecture.name: clamp_unit
module_architecture.role: Programmable command saturation and clamp-event indication stage.
responsibilities: Clamp command to the configured minimum and maximum bounds.
Assert clamp_active_out when saturation occurs.
Pass through valid commands unchanged when within bounds.
Provide a registered bounded command suitable for actuator driver logic.
interface_notes: Consumes command_in, command_valid_in, command_min_in, and command_max_in.
Produces command_out, command_valid_out, and clamp_active_out.
Clamp saturation pins the output to the nearest bound and asserts clamp_active_out for at least one cycle.
ownership_notes: Owns output command saturation behavior and the registered bounded command presented to actuator logic.
Ensures the actuator command output is bounded before it reaches the top-level output.

module_architecture.name: safety_supervisor
module_architecture.role: Safety aggregation, fallback enable generation, and sticky status management.
responsibilities: Monitor all safety-relevant conditions each cycle.
Assert stale_reject, timeout_fault, invalid_response, clamp_active, and fallback_active semantics.
Aggregate safety status bits into a compact output vector.
Hold sticky fault/status bits until cleared by host_clear_sticky or reset.
Inhibit model-derived actuation whenever fallback is required.
interface_notes: Consumes envelope_violation_in, response_stale_in, response_invalid_in, response_timeout_in, clamp_active_in, command_out_of_bounds_in, internal_fault_in, and host_clear_sticky.
Produces stale_reject_out, timeout_fault_out, invalid_response_out, clamp_active_out, fallback_active_out, safety_status_out, and sticky_status_out.
Fallback is asserted on timeout, stale response, malformed response, envelope violation, out-of-bounds command, or internal fault.
ownership_notes: Owns safety status bit generation and sticky state retention policy.
Provides the supervisory enable/holdoff signal used by request management and command selection.

module_architecture.name: telemetry_monitor
module_architecture.role: Synthesizable event counters and sticky status visibility for host observability.
responsibilities: Increment accepted response counter on valid accepted-response pulses.
Increment rejected stale counter on stale rejection pulses.
Increment clamp event counter on clamp saturation pulses.
Increment timeout counter on timeout pulses.
Increment fallback activation counter on fallback selection pulses.
Expose sticky status for host debug and software monitoring.
interface_notes: Consumes accepted_response_pulse, rejected_stale_pulse, clamp_event_pulse, timeout_event_pulse, fallback_activation_pulse, sticky_clear_in, and sticky_status_out.
Produces accepted_response_count_out, rejected_stale_count_out, clamp_event_count_out, timeout_event_count_out, and fallback_activation_count_out.
Telemetry logic is clocked by clk and does not create a combinational path to actuator_cmd.
ownership_notes: Owns observable counters for supervisory events and sticky visibility data.
Counters are monotonic until reset; sticky clear affects sticky bits only unless otherwise implemented by secure programming policy.

interface_summary.intent: Provide the outstanding transaction context needed to validate asynchronous responses against ID, sequence, and freshness rules.
Provide supervisory grant/hold behavior so that unsafe request launches are inhibited and fallback policy is coordinated.
Deliver only accepted model outputs to deterministic command synthesis.
Route response qualification failures into safety monitoring and fallback decision logic.
Account for accepted responses, stale rejections, and timeout events in telemetry counters.
Force fallback command selection when safety policy requires safe actuation.
Expose sticky safety state for observability.
Provide the deterministic model-derived or fallback command word to the saturation stage.
Report saturation events and provide the registered bounded command for bound monitoring.
Advance or clear outstanding transaction lifecycle according to the transaction/command contract.
Count clamp saturation events for host observability.
Count stale rejections and timeout events in telemetry.

data_flow_summary: Top-level qualification inputs and vehicle geometry metadata enter request_manager, which emits a request payload and captures request_id, request_seq, and request_timestamp when a launch is authorized.

The external model response arrives asynchronously at response_validator, which compares request ID, sequence, freshness, and payload format against the outstanding transaction context before producing any accepted drag_force, lift_force, surface_pressure, or flow_field_meta outputs.
Accepted response outputs feed command_synthesizer, which performs deterministic local command generation with no surrogate inference or GPU dependency.
The synthesized command passes through clamp_unit, which saturates the command to COMMAND_MIN and COMMAND_MAX and raises clamp_active when saturation occurs.
safety_supervisor monitors envelope compliance, response validity, timeout, clamp activity, command bounds, and internal faults, and asserts fallback_active when safe actuation is required.
fallback_active has priority in command_synthesizer, causing a deterministic safe fallback command to be selected whenever safety policy demands it.

telemetry_monitor counts accepted responses, stale rejections, clamp events, timeout events, and fallback activations, while sticky status is exposed for host visibility and cleared only by host_clear_sticky or reset.
The architecture preserves a registered actuator_cmd output and avoids a combinational path from model_response inputs directly to actuator outputs.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: All synchronous modules are clocked by clk. Telemetry, request management, response qualification, command synthesis, clamp behavior, and safety supervision are implemented as synthesizable clocked logic.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: On rst_n deassertion, all outstanding requests, response flags, counters, sticky status bits, and command outputs return to a safe known state. The default command after reset is the safe fallback command, actuator_cmd_valid deasserts, model_request_valid deasserts, and no outstanding transaction remains pending.

integration_notes: The design is control-and-supervision IP only and does not instantiate physics, surrogate inference, neural-network layers, or GPU logic.
The transaction interface is compatible with a remote NIM or ChipLoop GPU-worker model service accessed only through request/response messages.
The default operating envelope behavior is inclusive 20 to 55 m/s, with host-operating envelope inputs allowed to refine the range and host_fallback_route_en able to route the system into fallback.

Parameterization includes REQUEST_ID_WIDTH, SEQ_WIDTH, COMMAND_WIDTH, COMMAND_MIN, COMMAND_MAX, FRESHNESS_WINDOW_CYCLES, RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_CYCLES, and SAFE_FALLBACK_COMMAND for ASIC integration and secure programming use cases.

The architecture is suitable for the supplied automotive_aerodynamics integration context, including reference conditions of stream_velocity_mps = 38.89 and geometry_format = STL with geometry_source = DrivAerML reference geometry.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
